title: A Short History of Blasphemy in Britain (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上奇妙而有趣的知识，同时提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it's the start of a three-part mini-series, this time on the theme of blasphemy and free expression.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天是一档三集迷你系列的开篇，本集的主题是亵渎神明与言论自由。

sentences.en: In part one, this episode, we'll be talking about the history of blasphemy in Britain.
sentences.zh: 在第一部分也就是本集中，我们将探讨英国亵渎神明罪的历史。

sentences.en: Parts two and three will follow the story of the most famous blasphemy case in modern British history, the story of Salman Rushdie and the Satanic Verses.
sentences.zh: 第二部分和第三部分将讲述英国现代史上最著名的亵渎神明案，即 Salman Rushdie 与《The Satanic Verses》的故事。

sentences.en: It’s a story about a famous British author whose book was deemed so incendiary, so blasphemous, that the Supreme Leader of Iran issued a death sentence against him and he had to go into hiding for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于一位英国知名作家的故事，他的书被认为具有极大的煽动性、对神明极不敬，以至于伊朗最高领袖对下达了死刑令，迫使他隐匿长达 10 年之久。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们就不浪费时间，直接切入正题吧。

sentences.en: In January 1697, a young man named Thomas Aikenhead was sitting in a prison cell in Edinburgh, waiting to die.
sentences.zh: 1697 年 1 月，一个名叫 Thomas Aikenhead 的年轻人正坐在爱丁堡的一个监狱牢房里，等待死刑。

sentences.en: He was twenty years old, a student at the University of Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 他二十岁，是爱丁堡大学的一名学生。

sentences.en: His crime, for which he had been tried, convicted, and sentenced to hang by his neck until dead, was blasphemy.
sentences.zh: 他的罪名是亵渎神明，为此他经过审判、定罪，并被判处绞刑，直到死亡。

sentences.en: So, what exactly had he done? Well, he had done what many students around the world still do today.
sentences.zh: 那么，他到底做了什么呢？其实，他做的事很多世界各地的学生今天依然在做。

sentences.en: He had questioned what he had been told was true.
sentences.zh: 他对被告知是真理的东西提出了质疑。

sentences.en: He had made remarks to friends, in conversation, at a dinner.
sentences.zh: 他在与朋友的对话中、在晚宴上发表了一些言论。

sentences.en: He had called the Old Testament "Ezra's fables," suggesting that the first part of the Bible was no more reliable than a myth.
sentences.zh: 他把《旧约》称为“以斯拉的寓言”，暗示圣经的第一部分并不比神话更可靠。

sentences.en: He had described theology as, and I quote, “a rhapsody of ill-invented nonsense”.
sentences.zh: 他将神学描述为（我引用原话）“一首胡编乱造的无稽之谈狂想曲”。

sentences.en: He had suggested, at various points, that Jesus Christ was an impostor.
sentences.zh: 他在不同场合暗示耶稣基督是个骗子。

sentences.en: He had not published a pamphlet, or preached in a public square, or nailed anything to a church door.
sentences.zh: 他没有发表小册子，没有在公共广场上演讲，也没有把任何东西钉在教堂大门上。

sentences.en: He had floated these ideas to his friends.
sentences.zh: 他只是把这些想法向朋友们吐露了。

sentences.en: The problem was that these ideas were blasphemous.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，这些想法被视为亵渎神明。

sentences.en: On the 8th of January, 1697, Thomas Aikenhead was hanged.
sentences.zh: 1697 年 1 月 8 日，Thomas Aikenhead 被处以绞刑。

sentences.en: He was the last person executed for blasphemy in Britain.
sentences.zh: 他是英国最后一个因亵渎神明罪而被处决的人。

sentences.en: Now, it is tempting to think of this as a story from the distant past — the kind of thing that happened in a more primitive era, before science and reason arrived to improve the world.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们很容易把这当作一个遥远过去的故事——那种发生在科学和理性到来、改善世界之前那个更原始时代的事件。

sentences.en: But the distance is not as great as it might seem.
sentences.zh: 但这种距离并没有想象的那么遥远。

sentences.en: 1697 is not the Middle Ages. The Bank of England had been founded just a few years earlier.
sentences.zh: 1697 年并不是中世纪。英格兰银行就在几年前刚刚成立。

sentences.en: Isaac Newton's theories of motion and gravitation were ten years old.
sentences.zh: 艾萨克的运动和万有引力理论已经问世十年。

sentences.en: John Locke had recently published his famous Essay Concerning Human Understanding.
sentences.zh: John Locke 最近刚出版了他著名的《人类理解论》。

sentences.en: This was, by the standards of its time, a highly educated and rational society.
sentences.zh: 按当时的标准，这是一个高度受教育且理性的社会。

sentences.en: And yet it hanged a student for conversation.
sentences.zh: 然而，它却因为闲聊而绞死了一名学生。

sentences.en: That fact, and the long strange journey from that moment to the present, is what this episode is about.
sentences.zh: 这个事实，以及从那个时刻到现在的漫长而奇异的旅程，就是本集的主题。

sentences.en: So, to go back to its origins, “blasphemy” is a very old word, and where it comes from is important.
sentences.zh: 那么，回到它的起源，“blasphemy”（亵渎）是一个非常古老的词，它的出处很重要。

sentences.en: It comes from the Greek, blasphemia. The root blapt means to injure; and pheme means speech or reputation.
sentences.zh: 它源自希腊语 blasphemia。词根 blapt 意为伤害；pheme 意为言论或名誉。

sentences.en: Blasphemia, then, means roughly to speak harmfully of something, or to speak ill of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，Blasphemia 大致意为对某事恶语相向，或说其坏话。

sentences.en: And in its original Greek sense, it did not specifically mean speaking against God, or a religious deity.
sentences.zh: 在它最初的希腊语含义中，它并不特指针对上帝或宗教神明的言论。

sentences.en: It meant speaking harmfully about anyone or anything held in high regard.
sentences.zh: 它是指对任何受人高度尊敬的人或事物进行恶意中伤。

sentences.en: You could blaspheme a person, a king, or a reputation.
sentences.zh: 你可以亵渎一个人、一个国王或一种名誉。

sentences.en: When the word passed into English through Latin and Old French, it had already changed.
sentences.zh: 当这个词通过拉丁语和古法语传入英语时，它已经变味了。

sentences.en: Blasphemy now meant, specifically, speaking against God, against sacred things, against the teachings of the Church.
sentences.zh: 此时的亵渎特指反对上帝、反对神圣事物、反对教会教义的言论。

sentences.en: And the reason this was treated as a serious crime was not simply religious.
sentences.zh: 这种行为被当作严重罪行处理，原因不仅仅是宗教方面的。

sentences.en: It was political. In a society where the Church and the state were deeply connected, speaking against God was speaking against the order of the world.
sentences.zh: 它也是政治性的。在一个教会与国家深度绑定的社会里，反对上帝就是反对现行的世界秩序。

sentences.en: A king ruled by divine right. Courts relied on Christian oaths.
sentences.zh: 君王凭借神权统治。法庭依靠基督教誓言运作。

sentences.en: The law itself was intertwined with Christian assumptions about morality and order.
sentences.zh: 法律本身与关于道德和秩序的基督教假设交织在一起。

sentences.en: And this was made even more explicit in the XVI century when Henry VIII broke with Rome.
sentences.zh: 在 16 世纪亨利八世与罗马决裂时，这一点变得更加明确。

sentences.en: When he made himself the head of the Church of England, religious authority and political authority became one and the same.
sentences.zh: 当他让自己成为英格兰教会的领袖时，宗教权威与政治权威便合二为一了。

sentences.en: The Crown and the Church were fused.
sentences.zh: 王权与教会融合在了一起。

sentences.en: This meant that to challenge the Church was, effectively, to challenge the Crown.
sentences.zh: 这意味着挑战教会实际上就是挑战王权。

sentences.en: And that made blasphemy not just a sin, but something closer to rebellion.
sentences.zh: 这使得亵渎神明不仅是一种罪过，更接近于叛乱。

sentences.en: The law that developed around this was never tidy — there was no single act of Parliament that defined it — but its purpose was consistent.
sentences.zh: 围绕这一点制定的法律从来都不是井然有序的——没有哪一部单一的议会法案对其进行过定义——但它的目的是一贯的。

sentences.en: It protected the established Church of England and, by extension, the political order that rested upon it.
sentences.zh: 它保护了既定的英格兰教会，并由此延伸，保护了赖以建立的政治秩序。

sentences.en: That point will become very important later on.
sentences.zh: 这一点在后面会变得非常重要。

sentences.en: But set aside, for a moment, the question of which church the law was protecting.
sentences.zh: 但先暂时把法律保护的是哪一个教会这个问题放在一边。

sentences.en: There is a more basic question worth asking: why did it matter so much at all?
sentences.zh: 有一个更基本的问题值得一问：为什么这事在当时如此重要？

sentences.en: Why would a supposedly confident Christian society care so much about a few offensive words?
sentences.zh: 为什么一个自诩自信的基督教社会会如此在意区区几句冒犯的话？

sentences.en: Of course, people genuinely believed that the sacred mattered, and that they had a Christian duty to protect it.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们确实相信神圣至关重要，他们有保护神圣的基督教责任。

sentences.en: But private doubt was never the real target.
sentences.zh: 但私下的怀疑从来都不是真正的打击目标。

sentences.en: What the law cared about was public challenge: the pamphlet, the printing press, the speech in a public square.
sentences.zh: 法律真正在意的是公开的挑战：小册子、印刷机、广场上的演讲。

sentences.en: And those who faced the consequences were those who dared to challenge most openly.
sentences.zh: 而那些面临后果的人，正是那些敢于最公开挑战的人。

sentences.en: Percy Bysshe Shelley is a good example. Today he is remembered as one of England's greatest Romantic poets.
sentences.zh: Percy Bysshe Shelley 就是一个很好的例子。今天他被铭记为英国最伟大的浪漫主义诗人之一。

sentences.en: But in 1811, he was expelled from Oxford University for publishing a short pamphlet called "The Necessity of Atheism."
sentences.zh: 但在 1811 年，他因出版一本名为《无神论的必要性》的小册子而被牛津大学开除。

sentences.en: He and his co-author had sent the pamphlet to the heads of Oxford colleges and to several bishops, apparently hoping to start a debate.
sentences.zh: 他和合著者将这本小册子寄给了牛津各学院的负责人和几位主教，显然是希望能引发一场辩论。

sentences.en: What they started was a disciplinary hearing, and they were expelled the same afternoon.
sentences.zh: 然而他们引发的是一场纪律听证会，当天下午他们就被开除了。

sentences.en: And if Shelley shows what institutional punishment could look like, the experience of a man called Richard Carlile shows what happened when the criminal law was used more directly.
sentences.zh: 如果说 Shelley 展示了体制惩罚的形式，那么一个名叫 Richard Carlile 的人的经历则展示了当刑法被更直接地动用时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Carlile was a printer and political journalist who spent years in prison in the 1820s for publishing works considered blasphemous, including Thomas Paine's "The Age of Reason," which is a critique of the Bible and organised religion.
sentences.zh: Carlile 是一名印刷商兼政治记者，在 19 世纪 20 年代，他因出版被认为具有亵渎性的著作而在狱中度过了多年，其中包括 Thomas Paine 的《理性时代》，该书对圣经和有组织宗教进行了批判。

sentences.en: While Carlile was in prison, his wife and sister kept running the publishing shop in London.
sentences.zh: 当 Carlile 身处狱中时，他的妻子和妹妹继续在伦敦经营着那家印刷店。

sentences.en: They were also charged and imprisoned. Then volunteers came to keep the shop open.
sentences.zh: 她们也遭到起诉并被判入狱。接着志愿者们前来继续维持店铺运营。

sentences.en: They were imprisoned too. Carlile argued, explicitly, that blasphemy law was a political tool.
sentences.zh: 他们也被捕入狱。Carlile 明确指出，亵渎法是一个政治工具。

sentences.en: It was not being used to protect God; it was being used to protect the ruling class, which had built its authority on the claim that the social order was God's design.
sentences.zh: 它根本不是用来保护上帝的，而是用来保护统治阶级的，后者将其权威建立在“社会秩序是上帝的设计”这一主张之上。

sentences.en: To question the Bible was, in this reading, to question why some people owned land and others did not.
sentences.zh: 按照这种解读，质疑圣经就是质疑为什么有些人拥有土地而其他人没有。

sentences.en: Now, by the twentieth century, most people in Britain assumed that blasphemy law was effectively dead.
sentences.zh: 到了二十世纪，英国大多数人都认为亵渎法实际上已经名存实亡。

sentences.en: It hadn't been enforced in decades. Religious belief was in decline.
sentences.zh: 它已经几十年没有被执行过了。宗教信仰正在衰落。

sentences.en: Satirical publications were more than happy to poke fun at the church.
sentences.zh: 讽刺刊物非常乐意拿教会开玩笑。

sentences.en: The general feeling was that, as a society, we had moved past all that.
sentences.zh: 普遍的看法是，作为一个社会，我们已经超越了这一切。

sentences.en: In 1977, a woman named Mary Whitehouse proved that was not the case.
sentences.zh: 但在 1977 年，一个名叫 Mary Whitehouse 的女性证明事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Whitehouse was a campaigner for what she called moral standards in public life.
sentences.zh: Whitehouse 是一位致力于她所谓的公共生活道德标准的活动家。

sentences.en: She had spent years challenging what she saw as the moral decline of British television and publishing.
sentences.zh: 她花费数年时间挑战她眼中英国电视和出版业的道德沦丧。

sentences.en: In 1977, she brought a private prosecution against a newspaper called Gay News for publishing a poem called "The Love That Dares to Speak Its Name."
sentences.zh: 1977 年，她对一家名为《Gay News》的报纸提起了一起私人诉讼，起因是该报发表了一首名为《敢于说出名字的爱》的诗。

sentences.en: The poem was written by the academic James Kirkup.
sentences.zh: 这首诗由学者 James Kirkup 创作。

sentences.en: Now, you can find this poem online, but I have to warn you, it is quite explicit and not for the easily offended.
sentences.zh: 你现在可以在网上找到这首诗，但我必须提醒你，它相当露骨，不适合容易被冒犯的人。

sentences.en: It is written from the perspective of a homosexual Roman soldier who had been at the crucifixion, and it describes his erotic feelings towards the body of Christ.
sentences.zh: 它是从一个曾见证耶稣受难的同性恋罗马士兵的视角写的，描述了他对基督身体的肉欲感受。

sentences.en: Whitehouse argued this was blasphemous libel.
sentences.zh: Whitehouse 认为这是亵渎性的诽谤。

sentences.en: The case went to trial at the Old Bailey, England's most famous criminal court.
sentences.zh: 此案在英国最著名的刑事法院 Old Bailey 开庭审理。

sentences.en: The editor of Gay News, Denis Lemon, was convicted.
sentences.zh: 《Gay News》的主编 Denis Lemon 被判有罪。

sentences.en: He received a suspended prison sentence and a fine.
sentences.zh: 他被判处缓刑并处罚金。

sentences.en: This was 1977. The year of the Sex Pistols and the Queen's Silver Jubilee.
sentences.zh: 那是 1977 年。性手枪乐队成立以及女王登基银禧庆典的年份。

sentences.en: And yet a newspaper editor had been convicted for publishing a poem, under a law whose roots stretched back nearly three centuries.
sentences.zh: 然而，就在这一年，一名报纸编辑因为发表了一首诗而被定罪，依据的法律其根源可以追溯到近三个世纪前。

sentences.en: The reaction was fierce. For many people, especially in journalism and the arts, the conviction was an outrage.
sentences.zh: 社会反应极其强烈。对许多人来说，尤其是新闻界和艺术界，这次定罪简直是骇人听闻。

sentences.en: A poem was not a crime. Freedom of expression had to include the right to offend.
sentences.zh: 一首诗算不上犯罪。言论自由必须包括冒犯的权利。

sentences.en: For Whitehouse and her supporters, it was a statement that some things were beyond what a decent society should tolerate.
sentences.zh: 而在 Whitehouse 及其支持者看来，这表明有些东西超出了一个正派社会所能容忍的底线。

sentences.en: And two years later, in 1979, Monty Python released Life of Brian.
sentences.zh: 两年后的 1979 年，Monty Python 乐队推出了《Life of Brian》。

sentences.en: The film follows Brian of Nazareth, a man born in a stable next door to Jesus, who is constantly mistaken for the Messiah.
sentences.zh: 这部电影讲述了 Brian of Nazareth 的故事，他出生在耶稣隔壁的马棚里，却不断被误认为是弥赛亚。

sentences.en: The Church of England and the Catholic Church condemned it.
sentences.zh: 英格兰教会和天主教会都对这部电影进行了谴责。

sentences.en: Several local councils in Britain banned it outright.
sentences.zh: 英国的几个地方议会直接禁播了它。

sentences.en: Norway banned it altogether, which Swedish cinema posters exploited cheerfully, writing "So funny it was banned in Norway."
sentences.zh: 挪威则彻底禁播了它，瑞典的电影海报愉快地利用了这一点，上面写着“滑稽至极，以至于在挪威被禁”。

sentences.en: Now, Life of Brian was never prosecuted.
sentences.zh: 当然，《Life of Brian》从未被起诉。

sentences.en: But the Gay News case and the Life of Brian row showed that, in Britain in the late 1970s, the question of what could and couldn't be said about religion was still very much alive.
sentences.zh: 但《Gay News》案和《Life of Brian》的风波表明，在 20 世纪 70 年代末的英国，关于什么能说、什么不能说有关宗教的话题依然非常活跃。

sentences.en: And then, a decade later, everything shifted.
sentences.zh: 而在十年之后，一切都变了。

sentences.en: In September 1988, Salman Rushdie published a novel called The Satanic Verses.
sentences.zh: 1988 年 9 月，Salman Rushdie 出版了一部名为《The Satanic Verses》的小说。

sentences.en: The novel caused immediate and widespread offence among Muslim communities around the world.
sentences.zh: 这部小说在世界各地的穆斯林群体中引起了立即且广泛的冒犯感。

sentences.en: The full story of that controversy is what we'll cover in the next two episodes, so you’ll forgive me for only mentioning it in passing here.
sentences.zh: 这场争议的完整故事将在接下来的两集里探讨，所以请原谅我在这里仅顺便提及。

sentences.en: But one consequence of the protests and this uproar matters directly for the history of blasphemy law.
sentences.zh: 但抗议和这场喧嚣的一个后果直接关系到亵渎法的发展史。

sentences.en: When Muslim organisations in Britain looked for legal protection against the book, naturally, they turned to blasphemy law.
sentences.zh: 当英国的穆斯林组织寻求法律保护以抵御这本书时，他们自然而然地转向了亵渎法。

sentences.en: And here they discovered something remarkable.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他们发现了一件令人瞩目的事情。

sentences.en: The law was not available to them. English blasphemy law, as it had developed over three centuries, protected Christianity, specifically the Church of England.
sentences.zh: 这项法律并不适用于他们。正如三个世纪以来所发展的那样，英国的亵渎法保护的是基督教，尤其是英格兰教会。

sentences.en: It had never been extended to cover Islam, or Judaism, or any other faith.
sentences.zh: 它从未扩大到涵盖伊斯兰教、犹太教或任何其他信仰。

sentences.en: This was not a technicality. It revealed the real character of the law.
sentences.zh: 这并非技术细节问题。它暴露了法律的真实本质。

sentences.en: It had never been a neutral law protecting the sacred as such.
sentences.zh: 它从来都不是一项保护神圣本身的中立法律。

sentences.en: It was a structural feature of a law that had grown up as the legal arm of an established Christian state.
sentences.zh: 它是作为一个基督教国家的法律臂膀成长起来的法律体系的结构性特征。

sentences.en: Still, the implication was deeply uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这种含义令人感到极其不安。

sentences.en: British law was telling Muslim citizens that their faith deserved less legal protection than the faith of their Christian neighbours.
sentences.zh: 英国法律在告诉穆斯林公民，他们的信仰所获得的法律保护不如其基督教邻居的信仰。

sentences.en: For communities already dealing with racism, economic disadvantages, and often a sense that mainstream British society didn't understand them, this was more than a legal disappointment.
sentences.zh: 对于那些已经在应对种族主义、经济劣势，并且常常感到主流英国社会不理解他们的群体来说，这不仅仅是一个法律上的失望。

sentences.en: It confirmed something many had long suspected.
sentences.zh: 它证实了许多人长期以来的猜测。

sentences.en: And the debate that followed was long and difficult.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的辩论漫长而艰难。

sentences.en: Should blasphemy law be extended to cover all religions?
sentences.zh: 是否应该扩大亵渎法的范围以涵盖所有宗教？

sentences.en: That would give equal protection to Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and every other faith.
sentences.zh: 那将为伊斯兰教、犹太教、印度教以及其他所有信仰提供同等的保护。

sentences.en: But it would also make it far harder to criticise or satirise any of them.
sentences.zh: 但这也将使批评或讽刺其中任何一个宗教变得难上加难。

sentences.en: Or should the law be abolished altogether?
sentences.zh: 或者应该彻底废除这项法律？

sentences.en: The argument for abolition was that in a largely secular society with many different religions and beliefs, no set of ideas — however important to those who hold them — can be protected from challenge by law.
sentences.zh: 支持废除的论点是，在一个拥有多种不同宗教和信仰的世俗化社会中，没有任何一套思想——无论对持有者多么重要——能够免受法律挑战的保护。

sentences.en: You can protect people. You cannot protect ideas.
sentences.zh: 你可以保护人。你无法保护思想。

sentences.en: Parliament eventually chose abolition. The Criminal Justice and Immigration Act of 2008 ended blasphemy as a criminal offence in England and Wales.
sentences.zh: 议会最终选择了废除。《2008年刑事司法与移民法案》终结了英格兰和威尔士将亵渎神明作为刑事犯罪的历史。

sentences.en: The three-hundred-year experiment was over.
sentences.zh: 这场长达三百年的试验结束了。

sentences.en: And of course, Britain was not and has not been having these discussions in isolation.
sentences.zh: 当然，英国过去没有、现在也并非孤立地进行这些讨论。

sentences.en: The Danish cartoons controversy, and later the murders at Charlie Hebdo, were reminders that even where blasphemy is no longer a crime, offence to religion can still have enormous political and sometimes deadly consequences.
sentences.zh: 丹麦漫画争议，以及后来的查理周刊惨案，都在提醒人们：即使在亵渎不再是犯罪的地方，冒犯宗教仍可能带来巨大的政治后果，有时甚至是致命的后果。

sentences.en: And beyond Britain, the legal picture is still very uneven.
sentences.zh: 在英国之外，法律状况仍然很不均衡。

sentences.en: In some countries, especially Muslim-majority countries, blasphemy laws remain harsh, and in a few cases can carry the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 在一些国家，尤其是穆斯林人口占多数的国家，亵渎法依然严厉，少数情况下甚至可判处死刑。

sentences.en: In others, there may be no formal blasphemy law as such, but there are still laws against insulting religion, offending religious feelings, or disturbing religious peace.
sentences.zh: 在其他国家，可能没有形式上的亵渎法本身，但仍然存在禁止侮辱宗教、冒犯宗教感情或破坏宗教和平的法律。

sentences.en: Now, bringing it back to Britain, you might think that abolishing blasphemy law in 2008 settled the question.
sentences.zh: 好了，把话题拉回英国，你可能会认为 2008 年废除亵渎法已经解决了这个问题。

sentences.en: It didn't. In November 2024 — less than two years ago — a Labour MP named Tahir Ali stood up at Prime Minister's Questions and asked the Prime Minister, Keir Starmer, to introduce laws prohibiting the " desecration " of religious texts and the prophets of the Abrahamic religions.
sentences.zh: 并没有。在 2024 年 11 月——不到两年前——一名工党议员 Tahir Ali 在首相质询环节站起来，要求首相 Keir Starmer 引入禁止“亵渎”宗教文本以及亚伯拉罕诸教先知的法律。

sentences.en: In other words: a new blasphemy law. The timing was deliberate.
sentences.zh: 换句话说：一项新的亵渎法。这个时机是刻意挑选的。

sentences.en: Ali was speaking during Islamophobia Awareness Month, and his target was clear — protection for Islam, in particular, from public mockery and insult.
sentences.zh: Ali 发言时正值伊斯兰恐惧症宣传月，他的目标很明确——特别是要求保护伊斯兰教免受公众嘲笑和侮辱。

sentences.en: And specifically, making burning the Quran a criminal act.
sentences.zh: 具体而言，就是将焚烧《古兰经》定为刑事犯罪。

sentences.en: Starmer's initial response did not include a clear no.
sentences.zh: Starmer 最初的回应并没有明确说不。

sentences.en: He said that " desecration is awful" and that his government was " committed to tackling all forms of hatred and division."
sentences.zh: 他表示“亵渎是可怕的”，并且他的政府“致力于打击一切形式的仇恨和分裂”。

sentences.en: This non-answer caused immediate alarm, because it stopped short of a clear rejection.
sentences.zh: 这种非回答式的表态立即引起了恐慌，因为它没有明确拒绝。

sentences.en: The National Secular Society wrote to the government to demand a clear rejection.
sentences.zh: 英国国家世俗协会致信政府，要求予以明确拒绝。

sentences.en: Journalists and commentators across the political spectrum expressed concern.
sentences.zh: 跨政治谱系的记者和评论员都表达了担忧。

sentences.en: A few weeks later, the government clarified its position.
sentences.zh: 几周后，政府澄清了立场。

sentences.en: A minister stated that the government would in fact "completely rule out " re-introducing blasphemy laws.
sentences.zh: 一位大臣表示，政府事实上将“完全排除”重新引入亵渎法的可能性。

sentences.en: So, to wrap things up, for centuries, blasphemy law in Britain was never really about protecting all faith equally.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，几个世纪以来，英国的亵渎法从来都不是真正为了平等地保护所有信仰。

sentences.en: It was about protecting the religious foundations of public order.
sentences.zh: 它是为了保护公共秩序的宗教基础。

sentences.en: And once Britain stopped being a uniformly Christian society, these laws began to look not only old, but unfair.
sentences.zh: 一旦英国不再是一个清一色的基督教社会，这些法律不仅开始显得陈旧，而且显得不公平。

sentences.en: But still, questions about religious protection are as present as ever.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于宗教保护的问题依然和以往一样现实。

sentences.en: Where does criticism of a religion end, and where does incitement against its followers begin?
sentences.zh: 对一个宗教的批评在哪里结束，针对其信徒的煽动又在哪里开始？

sentences.en: How much offence must a free society be willing to tolerate?
sentences.zh: 一个自由社会必须愿意容忍多大程度的冒犯？

sentences.en: And who gets to decide? These are old questions, but they have not stayed in the past.
sentences.zh: 谁来决定？这些都是老问题，但它们并没有留在过去。

sentences.en: The language has changed. The laws have changed.
sentences.zh: 语言变了。法律变了。

sentences.en: Britain itself has changed. Fortunately, my country no longer hangs students for saying the wrong things at dinner, but we still have not fully settled how a free society should respond to the sacred.
sentences.zh: 英国本身也变了。幸运的是，我的国家不再因为人们在晚餐时说错了话而将学生绞死，但对于一个自由社会应该如何回应神圣，我们仍未完全达成共识。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on the history of blasphemy in Britain.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于英国亵渎神明历史的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: As a reminder, this is part one of a three-part mini-series.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，这是三集迷你系列的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up, in part two and three, we tell the story of Salman Rushdie and The Satanic Verses — the book itself, the protests, the fatwa, the public debate, the assassination attempts, and the questions it got people asking about freedom of expression.
sentences.zh: 接下来，在第二部分和第三部分中，我们将讲述 Salman Rushdie 与《The Satanic Verses》的故事——这本书本身、抗议活动、法特瓦教令、公众辩论、暗杀未遂，以及它引发人们对言论自由的思考。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目见。
